title: FreeMask: Synthetic Images with Dense Annotations Make Stronger Segmentation Models
mechanism: Generate images from semantic masks, drop synthetic pixels whose loss under a real-trained model exceeds a per-class threshold, and generate more samples for harder masks.
adaptation: Filter synthetic EL pairs with the house ensemble's per-class loss (crack threshold set on train-cell loss, allowing 2 px jitter); hardness per mask = per-cell crack/inactive loss of the house model on train; applies to every synthetic arm in this direction.
min_experiment: Arm: synthetic stream (row 1 or 2) with filtering + hardness resampling. Baseline: same stream unfiltered, PF, 5 seeds. Metric: the arm's main metric (E1 relF1@2 or CV inactive IoU). Kill: gain < +0.01.
evidence: R (from web summary of the paper): ADE20K 48.7 -> 52.0 mIoU with filtered synthetic data jointly or as pretraining; synthetic-only 48.3 vs real 48.5.
